ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and key officers against the South African National Treasury sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, United States OFAC SDN list, United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Financial Intelligence Centre's targeted financial sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for all foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), including their family members and close associates. The screening must be documented under a FICA-compliant risk-based approach and must include ongoing transaction monitoring and adverse media review. The responsible accountable institution must maintain written AML/CFT policies consistent with FATF Recommendations 10, 11, and 12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal at www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in English or Afrikaans, using Latin-alphabet characters. A proposed name may include a transliteration into the Latin alphabet from another language. The name must comply with the Companies Act 71 of 2008, section 11, and must not be false, misleading, offensive, or contrary to public policy. The full legal name must include the suffix '(Pty) Ltd' or 'Proprietary Limited'. Where a shortened name is used, it must still be registered and clearly distinguishable from existing names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may apply for reconsideration through the CIPC e-Services portal within 30 days of the rejection notice. The reconsideration application must state the grounds of appeal and include supporting evidence demonstrating that the name is distinctive, not confusingly similar to existing registered names, and not otherwise prohibited under the Companies Act. If the CIPC maintains the refusal, the applicant may initiate a formal complaint with the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and thereafter seek judicial review in the High Court. For sensitive tokens, an applicant may seek written ministerial or regulatory consent from the relevant authority (e.g., SARB or FSCA) to use restricted words and provide that consent during reconsideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office for an Electronic Money Institution. The Companies Act requires a registered office to be a physical address in South Africa capable of receiving service of legal process. Additionally, SARB and FSCA licensing requirements demand substantive physical presence in South Africa, including a board, executive management, compliance function, and operational infrastructure. A registered address may be provided by a professional corporate service provider, but the physical office must be genuine and not merely a virtual post office box address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — 90% likelihood of pre-licensing premises inspection and 80-90% likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspections by the SARB Prudential Authority, FSCA, or Financial Intelligence Centre post-licensing. An EMI's on-site inspection risk is materially higher than ordinary private companies due to the high-risk licensed financial services classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, Chapter 6 (Formation of Companies), sections 12-19, 23 and 40; read with the Companies Regulations, 2011, and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) – Corporate Filing e-Services Portal, Pretoria
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A standard MOI or bespoke MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; shares may be issued for any consideration determined by the directors (s. 40); no escrow deposit or capital verification certificate is required at incorporation; issued share capital and classes must be stated in the MOI and share certificates must be issued upon allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription and allotment of 100 ordinary shares of ZAR 1.00 each to the founding subscriber be and is hereby approved; (2) the registered office located in Johannesburg, Gauteng, be and is hereby adopted as the company's domicilium citandi et executandi; (3) [Director A] be and is hereby appointed as sole Director and Managing Director, with authority to execute banking mandates and statutory filings; (4) [Officer B] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer; (5) the directors are authorized to open corporate bank accounts and to apply for all regulatory licenses including the Electronic Money Issuer authorization. This resolution is final and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Registration Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free online name search on the CIPC company search registry; if the desired name is available, file Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Name) electronically; reserve one primary name and one alternative name; ensure that the proposed name does not conflict with registered companies, domain names, or trademarks; verify that the proposed business objects correspond to ISIC 6619 (auxiliary financial services – electronic money issuing) for consistency in later regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 – Application for Reservation of Name
Certified copy of each applicant director's identity document or passport
Proposed company objects and industry classification (ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522110)
Anticipated jurisdiction of registered office (province and city)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or placed in a query cycle, file an amended CoR 9.1 with corrected particulars within CIPC's prescribed response period; alternatively, register the company under its registration number and apply for a name change at a later stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Incorporation Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and CIPC-authorized incorporator or registered representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation using the standard Form CoR 15.1A or a bespoke MOI that specifies the authorized share classes, voting rights, director appointments, and quorum rules; complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) with particulars of the incorporator, first directors, registered office address, and business objects; obtain signed consents to act as director from each appointee (Form CoR 14.1B); prepare a beneficial ownership schedule identifying all natural persons that will hold or control share interests of 5% or more.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 – Notice of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A or bespoke MOI)
Form CoR 14.1B – Consent to Act as Director (executed by each director)
Beneficial ownership schedule and AML/KYC supporting evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any content defects identified by CIPC's verification engine, such as inconsistent share amounts, missing director signatures, or incomplete beneficial ownership data; resubmit the entire dossier electronically and maintain a fully executed original paper trail for audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to CIPC and Payment of Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Portal – Online Filing and Payment Gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services, select Company Registration, upload the incorporation dossier (CoR 14.1, MOI, director consents, beneficial ownership schedule) in PDF form; pay the prescribed registration fee and name reservation fee through the online payment gateway; retain the payment receipt, tax invoice, and transaction tracking number; monitor the filing status until CIPC moves the application to the 'Registered' or 'Entered' status; upon registration, download the CIPC Registration Certificate and the company's registration number.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 – Notice of Incorporation (final version)
Memorandum of Incorporation (final version)
CoR 14.1B – Consents to act as director
Beneficial ownership schedule
Proof of payment (CIPC tax invoice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a data verification query or rejection, file a corrective amendment within 10 business days via the 'Amend/Resubmit' function; for technical payment failures, escalate to the CIPC Contact Centre and obtain a service request number; if the 20-business-day statutory turnaround is exceeded, lodge a written escalation request online to expedite processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Post-Incorporation Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the MOI; adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution approving the subscription and allotment of shares, the adoption of the registered office address as the domicilium citandi et executandi, and the appointment of the Managing Director, Company Secretary, and Compliance Officer; record the minutes of the meeting in the company minute book; issue share certificates to the subscribers; open the statutory registers, including the share register, directors' register, and prescribed officers' register.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting (and agenda)
Pro-forma First Board Resolution (executed)
Directors' consents to act
Share subscription agreements and issued share certificates
Statutory register templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failing a quorum, obtain a written resolution signed by all directors/shareholders in lieu of a meeting; if a director declines appointment, substitute a qualified director before registration filings are updated; any defect in share allotment is cured by a ratified written shareholders' resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and UIF/COIDA Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour (DEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company on SARS eFiling to obtain an income tax reference number; simultaneously register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), UIF, and Skills Development Levy if employees will be engaged; register with the Compensation Fund on the DEL COIDA online portal; if taxable supplies exceed the VAT threshold, apply for VAT registration; provide trade classification code 6619, the CIPC registration certificate, and bank account confirmation to SARS
required_dossiers: CIPC registration certificate (CoR 14.1 endorsement)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents of directors and public officer
Corporate bank account confirmation
Registered office and postal addresses
Pro-forma employment records if staff engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS returns the registration to 'Inactive' status or rejects the translation, correct the omitted or inconsistent fields (trade classification code, address, or public officer appointment) and resubmit via eFiling; escalate to a SARS branch appointment if electronic resolution fails; for COIDA, appeal a classification assessment or file a corrected employee declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Register Compliance and CIPC Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC and company board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the prescribed period after incorporation, file the Beneficial Ownership Register schedule with CIPC under the General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; maintain an internal register identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds 5% or more of the shares or control rights in the company; update the register and refile on any change of beneficial ownership; attach the required verifiable KYC evidence to the internal record.
required_dossiers: Beneficial Ownership Register (company internal record)
CIPC beneficial ownership schedule (electronic filing)
Certified identity documents of beneficial owners
Proof of control or ownership structure chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects the beneficial ownership schedule due to incomplete particulars, correct the identity details with supporting documentation and refile immediately; if the schedule is not yet due, file an explanatory notice and monitor the CIPC compliance calendar; escalate material disputes to a CIPC compliance officer or external legal counsel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Prudential Authority of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB), in coordination with the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and the National Payment System Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorisation/Registration as an Electronic Money Issuer under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 and the SARB Position Paper on Electronic Money (including virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), Environmental Impact Assessment and Licensing Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No listed activity under the EIA Regulations of 2014 (Listing Notices 1, 2 and 3) applies to office-based digital financial technology operations; no full EIA or basic assessment required in the absence of a physical industrial structure, wastewater discharge, or emission-generating facility
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not directly applicable to a virtual IBAN/digital wallet business; where leased office premises generate domestic sewage, discharge to municipal sewer must comply with the National Water Act 36 of 1998, SANS 10400 Part P, and municipal bylaws; electronic waste disposal and server/ICT cooling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 and occupational exposure limits for electrical/thermal hazards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local Fire and Rescue Department under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400 Part T); structural load inspection certificate for the leased office floor space confirming rated floor loading; electric fence or building electrical compliance certificate (COC) per the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; workplace risk assessment, emergency evacuation plan, and occupational health clearance certificates before staff deployment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national tax authority; online portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); official site: www.sars.gov.za. Exchange control (FX repatriation) is administered separately by the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) through Authorized Dealers (commercial banks).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); the CIPC enterprise number is auto-linked to SARS and a provisional income tax reference number (ITREF) is issued at incorporation. Step 2: Complete registration on SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch: Income Tax (IT77), VAT (VAT101 — ten-digit VAT vendor number), and, if staff are hired, PAYE/UIF/SDL (EMP101). Step 3: Foreign shareholders and directors obtain their own South African tax reference numbers (non-resident individuals and foreign companies register with SARS directly). Step 4: Obtain the regulatory authorisations conditioning commencement of the EMI business: SARB Prudential Authority / FSCA authorisation under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 and FinSurv Authorized Dealer (Category II) approval for FX/SEPA/IBAN payment activities; each licence application requires a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN. Step 5: VAT registration must be completed within 21 days of exceeding the ZAR 1 million turnover threshold; failure to register within the statutory window attracts administrative non-compliance penalties of up to ZAR 4,000 per month (TAA s 210) plus an understatement penalty if tax shortfalls result.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a (Pty) Ltd incorporated in South Africa is automatically a resident taxpayer (Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, s 1 'resident' definition) taxed on worldwide income at the corporate rate of 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023). No pass-through or partnership transparency applies; profits are taxed at entity level and dividends paid are subject to Dividends Tax of 20% withheld at shareholder level. Capital gains: 80% of net gains are taxable at 27% (effective 21.6% corporate CGT). No territorial ring-fence, no tax-exempt zone; the CFC regime (s 9D) may tax undistributed offshore profits. The EMI's operating income — float margin, interchange fees, virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet management fees — is ordinary revenue fully taxable in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no 'check-the-box' entity-classification election. Available statutory elections and hybrid-mismatch safeguards: (1) Small Business Corporation status (s 12E) — electable on the annual return for qualifying (Pty) Ltd companies with gross income under ZAR 20 million, not more than five natural-person shareholders and under 20% passive income; progressive rates 0% to 27%. (2) Headquarter Company election (s 9I) — available where at least 80% of the company's interest is held in foreign companies (with foreign shareholding exceeding ZAR 5 million); provides relief for foreign dividends, interest, royalties and service fees, and foreign capital gains. (3) VAT grouping election (s 50, VAT Act) — a group of companies linked by at least 75% ownership may elect to be one VAT vendor. (4) CFC high-tax exemption election (s 9D(9)) — excludes CFC income that bears foreign tax of at least 18% (effective rate). (5) Hybrid mismatch rules (effective 1 January 2021) are self-executing anti-avoidance provisions that neutralise deductions for hybrid payments; no opt-out election exists. (6) Global Minimum Top-up Tax (Pillar Two, effective for fiscal years commencing on or after 31 December 2023, enacted in the Global Minimum Tax Act 2024) is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million; the domestic top-up tax is filed with SARS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; tax invoices and input-tax credit mechanism; financial services (including payment and wallet services) are generally exempt supplies under s 2 unless supplied to non-residents, in which case they may be zero-rated under s 11(2)(l).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 — compulsory registration within 21 days of exceeding R1 million taxable turnover in any 12-month period (VAT Act s 23(1)); voluntary registration is available once annual turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000. Exempt financial services count toward the turnover threshold. Note: Budget 2025 proposes lowering the compulsory threshold to ZAR 500,000 with effect from 1 April 2026 (not yet enacted).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or mandatory government API invoice-authorisation regime operates in South Africa. Electronic tax invoices are statutorily valid if they comply with s 20 of the VAT Act and are authentic, legible and retained for 5 years. SARS is progressively modernising e-invoicing toward PEPPOL-based interoperability and B2B e-invoicing via its eFiling APIs, but clearance remains return-based (monthly or bi-monthly VAT201 filings) rather than per-invoice authorisation. EMI-specific: the payment-scheme settlement statements (Central Bank Clearing / SEPA) and SWIFT MT103 messages constitute the audit trail supporting VAT records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Financial services supplied by the EMI to a non-resident are zero-rated under s 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act when: (i) the supplier is a VAT vendor carrying on an enterprise; (ii) the recipient is a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time the services are rendered; (iii) the services are not supplied directly in connection with land or movable property situated in South Africa; (iv) the services are not entertainment services; and (v) the vendor holds and retains documentary proof of the non-resident status and absence from South Africa at the time of supply. Qualifying zero-rated services: issuance of virtual IBANs, digital-wallet reserve management, cross-border payment processing and SEPA credits supplied to non-resident clients. The same services supplied to a South African resident would be exempt financial services (s 2) with restricted input-VAT recovery, subject to the s 17(1) de minimis relief where exempt financial supplies do not exceed ZAR 5,000 per month or 5% of monthly taxable supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable — no Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) or Bill of Lading for intangible or financial-service exports; the following documentary bundle applies instead.
Signed export service contract / service-level agreement with the non-resident client, evidencing place of supply, consideration and SEPA/IBAN payment mechanics.
SARS-compliant tax invoice (s 20 VAT Act) expressly reflecting zero-rating under s 11(2)(l).
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the Authorized Dealer, or SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation, evidencing receipt of foreign-currency settlement.

Non-resident status evidence: foreign tax residency certificate issued by the client's revenue authority, or a sworn declaration (Form F178 / FinSurv FEC declaration) confirming the client was outside South Africa at the time of supply.
Underlying transaction records: virtual IBAN issuance register, wallet ledger extracts and central-bank-clearing/SEPA settlement confirmations reconciled to the invoiced consideration.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Substantiation is high-risk: SARS and FinSurv review export-of-services positions for (i) misuse of s 11(2)(l), (ii) round-tripping of funds through the EMI's offshore wallets, and (iii) late or non-repatriation of foreign currency. Consequences of incorrect zero-rating or documentary failure: (1) additional VAT assessment at 15% on the full consideration plus statutory interest at the repo rate plus 3.5 percentage points per annum (s 39 VAT Act; s 187 TAA); (2) TAA understatement penalties (ss 222-223): 10% (substantial understatement), 25% (failure to take reasonable care), 50% (no reasonable grounds), 75% (impermissible avoidance), 150% (intentional tax evasion); (3) fraudulent zero-rating (e.g., forged non-resident declarations) attracts additional tax of up to 200% of the VAT shortfall under s 59(3) VAT Act, and criminal prosecution under TAA ss 233-235 with fines and imprisonment of up to 10 years for serious tax crimes (Schedule 1 TAA); (4) retrospective clawback: SARS may reopen assessments within 3 years of the original assessment, extended to 5 years for non-disclosure or negligence, and indefinitely where fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of material facts is established (s 99 TAA); (5) FinSurv exchange-control violations for failure to repatriate within 180 days may result in administrative penalties and criminal sanction under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Prudential Authority for bank and payment-system licensing and through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) for Exchange Control Regulations under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933). The National Payment System Act, 1998 (Act 78 of 1998), administered by the National Payment System Department, governs clearing, settlement and e-money issuance; SARB publishes the Position Paper on Electronic Money (revised 2024) which conditions non-bank e-money issuance on SARB authorisation, segregated reserve accounts at an Authorised Dealer (AD) bank, and full backing of e-money liabilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a single-floating-rand regime with dual-tier exchange control: current-account payments (trade, services, dividends, royalties, interest, management fees) are generally convertible through an Authorised Dealer (AD) without FinSurv pre-approval, subject to corroborating documentation, tax clearance and the SARB purpose-of-payment code framework; capital-account items (inward equity, shareholder loans, outward investment) remain subject to FinSurv approval or delegated AD limits. Profit remittance hurdles for a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI): (i) dividends must be declared from realised distributable reserves evidenced by audited or reviewed financial statements; (ii) the company must hold a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN with no outstanding returns and must withhold 20% dividends tax (s64G of the Income Tax Act, 1962, subject to double-taxation-agreement relief); (iii) the remitted funds must be traceable to foreign capital imported through an AD and classified as 'external funds', with the inward transfer declaration correctly filed; and (iv) non-resident shareholders must be accurately recorded in the share register and the CIPC beneficial-ownership filing to permit clean dividend outflow. No general prior approval is required for inward equity capital below sectoral thresholds, but the AD must apply FICA verification and sanctions screening before releasing funds as convertible external capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 3(1) in terms of the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933, a resident exporter must receive full export proceeds within 180 days from the date of shipment (or completion of services for services exports) and must repatriate such proceeds to South Africa. Since 1 January 2010, there is no mandatory conversion ratio: all or part of the proceeds may be retained in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with a South African AD bank, or converted to ZAR at the ruling market rate, at the exporter's election. Any foreign-currency receipts credited to the EMI's onshore accounts, including stablecoin conversions and nostro FCA balances attributable to cross-border services, must be repatriated within the same 180-day window and reported on the relevant FCA and inward-transfer returns. Merchanting trade (triangulation) and retention of proceeds offshore require prior FinSurv approval; default triggers exchange-control penalties and, in egregious cases, criminal prosecution under the Currency and Exchanges Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank and Rand Merchant Bank divisions)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, section 33(1) read with regulation 38)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; recurring annually on the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing flags the company as non-compliant and removes 'good standing'; the company cannot obtain a compliance certificate or access certain CIPC services; after two consecutive years of outstanding annual returns, CIPC may commence administrative deregistration (strike-off) under section 82(4) of the Companies Act; reinstatement thereafter requires a formal application and payment of CIPC reinstatement fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Register and Annual BO Declaration (Companies Amendment Regulations 2023; section 56A of the Companies Act 2008 as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: BO confirmation is filed annually together with the CIPC Annual Return within 30 business days of the incorporation anniversary; any direct or indirect shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to CIPC within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or confirm BO details results in rejection of the Annual Return and automatic non-compliant status; directors and beneficial owners may be held personally liable; continued non-compliance is a statutory offence under the Companies Act 2008 as amended and may lead to exclusion from the regulated e-money licence under SARB supervision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) approved by the board and delivered to shareholders (Companies Act 2008, section 30(4); section 33(2) if audited)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; CIPC if audited and compulsory filing applies; SARB Prudential Authority for the licensed e-money institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year for shareholder delivery; audited AFS filed with CIPC and SARB on the same six-month timeline where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors breach section 30/31 duties and commit a statutory offence; CIPC may issue a compliance notice or apply for a court order; for the e-money institution, SARB may attach licence conditions, impose a corrective directive, or suspend/withdraw the National Payment System authorisation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and provisional tax submissions (Income Tax Act No. 58 of 1962; Tax Administration Act No. 28 of 2011)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 due within 12 months after the financial year-end, subject to the annual SARS public notice; provisional tax payments due at the six-month and financial year-end anniversary dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may impose an administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act, additional tax for under-estimation of provisional payments, and interest at the prescribed rate; persistent default can trigger criminal sanctions, SARS civil collection, or liquidation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: National Payment System Annual Compliance and E-Money Reserve Verification Return (per SARB licence conditions and National Payment System Act No. 78 of 1998)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Reserve Bank - National Payment System Department and Prudential Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing within 30 business days after the financial year-end, or as expressly specified in the SARB authorisation and licence conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Adverse regulatory finding and formal directive to remedy; persistent default may result in suspension or withdrawal of the e-money issuance authorisation; referral to the Financial Intelligence Centre for AML/CFT enforcement and potential criminal prosecution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies Act 2008, section 34(2) read with regulation 28(2): compulsory independent audit if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; independent review required if the PIS is between 100 and 349; no statutory audit or review required if PIS is below 100 unless the Memorandum of Incorporation or an applicable regulatory licence imposes one. For a licensed electronic money institution, SARB will in any event require an annual independent audit of the entire entity and the e-money reserve pool under the National Payment System licensing framework.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; eligible fintech enterprise may benefit from the R&D tax incentive (section 11D of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962) allowing 150% deduction on qualifying research and development expenditure, and the general deduction of capital allowances under section 12C/12E for movable assets used in digital infrastructure; annual turnover under ZAR 20 million may qualify for small business corporation rates (0% to 21%) under section 12E, but the licensed EMI with substantial scale will ordinarily be taxed at the standard 27% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Income Tax Return) e-filed via SARS eFiling (https://efiling.sars.gov.za) or through a registered tax practitioner / SARS branch office
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with provisional tax payments required twice a year for companies whose gross income exceeds ZAR 1 million)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed annually by the statutory due date; for companies with a February year-end it is mid-January of the following year, and for other year-ends provisional deadlines apply, typically within 12 months after year-end as assessed per SARS notice; provisional tax payments are due six months after the start of year of assessment (first provisional) and at the end of the year of assessment (second provisional), with a third top-up payment optional.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter South African company registration number (e.g. 2022/123456/07).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned (Pty) Ltd must still enter its local registration number; non-resident shareholder details are captured in supporting schedules, not on this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter SARS income tax reference number assigned to the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the tax reference number issued to the South African branch or subsidiary; non-resident parent has a separate reference only if it has South African tax presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the close of the annual financial period (usually last day of February for South African companies unless SARS approved a different year-end).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned entities must align with the South African fiscal year unless a special ruling was obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report worldwide gross income of the South African resident company, including fees for virtual IBAN issuance, wallet interchange fees, float investment income, and other transactional revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned local subsidiary, report only income sourced in South Africa unless a controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution or permanent establishment rule applies; for a non-resident that is not a resident, only gross income attributable to a South African PE is taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest income from South African banks up to the exemption threshold only if the entity qualifies as a non-resident or in specific identified circumstances; in practice the (Pty) Ltd reports all interest and dividends unless exempt under section 10 or section 10B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are not automatically exempt; only the interest exemption in section 10(1)(h) applies to non-residents on amounts paid by SARS-approved financial institutions, but careful analysis of source and specifically exempt amounts is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter assessable income after exemptions but before trade deductions, capital gains inclusion and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a PE, assessable income shall be only the profits attributable to the PE; local head-office cost allocations must satisfy the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct expenditure actually incurred in the production of income under section 11(a), including salaries, cloud infrastructure costs, regulatory fees, licensing amortisation, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred by the head office outside South Africa and recharged to the branch are deductible only if they are supported by a transfer pricing documentation file and are arm's length, otherwise SARS will disallow under section 31 and section 23.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net taxable income after all deductions and allowable capital losses (limited to set-offs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure no offset of foreign head-office losses against South African PE profits unless permitted under the DTA and local law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 27% corporate rate to taxable income. Example: taxable income ZAR 10,000,000 → normal tax ZAR 2,700,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same 27% rate applies to a South African branch of a non-resident (including a foreign EMI parent), with branch profits tax potentially being due under the Income Tax Act unless exempted by treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim a credit under section 6quat for foreign taxes paid on income sourced outside South Africa that is also included in South African taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent cannot claim s 6quat credit on income of the South African subsidiary; only the subsidiary can claim in respect of its own foreign source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List the two (or three) provisional payments made, compute the balance of tax payable after payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled companies must still comply with provisional tax if estimated taxable income exceeds the statutory threshold; directors are personally liable for interest where estimates are intentionally understated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report 80% of net capital gain on disposal of capital assets; for companies an inclusion rate of 80% applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are taxed on capital gains only where the underlying asset constitutes immovable property situated in South Africa or assets of a PE, so the virtual financial services business's foreign intellectual property sale may be outside SARS's reach unless used through a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare intercompany transactions with foreign and domestic connected persons, including fees for technology licensing, management fees, and treasury services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent financing a South African subsidiary must ensure interest rates and loan terms are aligned with arm's length rates; the declaration must specify the method used (CUP, TNMM, etc.) under the SARS TP return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of ZAR 250 per month or part thereof for each month the return remains outstanding, up to a maximum of ZAR 2,500; understatement penalty under Tax Administration Act may be as high as 150% of the shortfall if the understatement is made intentionally or due to gross negligence; 10% additional tax on defaulters under section 213; interest (currently 10.5% per annum, adjusted quarterly) accrues on outstanding tax from the effective date until payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends paid by a South African resident company to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable DTA (e.g. 5% under the South Africa–Netherlands, South Africa–UK, South Africa–Mauritius and similar treaties on direct substantial shareholdings); the (Pty) Ltd must withhold and pay over DWT to SARS within 30 days of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief the beneficial owner of the dividend must (i) obtain a residency certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, (ii) complete and submit SARS Declaration DTD (Electing for relief from Dividends Tax) or the specific SARS form (e.g. DTD1) and provide the TRC to the paying company before the dividend payment; the payer retains the documentation in its records; the effective reduced rate will apply only where the shareholder holds at least 10% of the shares and the holding period conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties paid by a South African resident to non-residents: 15% withholding tax on royalties (section 49B of the Act), reduced to 0% under many treaties where the royalty is beneficially owned by a resident of the other state (e.g. DTA with the Netherlands, UK, Mauritius often 0% for royalties); statutory rate for interest paid by a South African resident to non-residents: 15% withholding tax on interest (section 49B), generally reduced to 0% under many tax treaties (e.g. South Africa-Netherlands 0% interest, beneficial ownership requirement applies); a domestic exemption applies for interest paid to a non-resident bank or a recognised financial institution on approved loans, provided certain requirements are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: South Africa has no universal turnover threshold exempting a company from preparing transfer pricing documentation, but SARS requires full TP documentation to be kept where cross-border connected-person transactions exceed ZAR 5 million in gross income or deductions in a year of assessment; Master File and Local File are required consistent with the OECD TP Guidelines, with specific practical thresholds: Local File is recommended for transactions above ZAR 5 million and Master File is required for MNE groups with a consolidated group revenue exceeding ZAR 1 billion, regardless of the local transaction value.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not maintain annual Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in the UAE or Cayman Islands, but economic substance is enforceable through (i) the general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) in section 103 of the Income Tax Act which permit SARS to disregard a transaction lacking commercial substance, (ii) the CFC rules in section 9D which attribute passive income derived by a controlled foreign company unless the CFC carries on substantial economic substance in its jurisdiction, (iii) case law and law of place of effective management (POEM); an EMI (Pty) Ltd must show real operations, banking licence, staff, treasury decisions, and technology development in South Africa, or risk having its transactions recharacterised and its tax residency or entitlement to treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Understatement of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting income from transaction fees, float interest, or virtual wallet commissions; inflating deductions; creating fictitious expenses; using undisclosed foreign bank accounts or crypto-currency conduits to hide revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall under Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 s 223; additional interest; criminal conviction under s 235 and s 104(1) of the TAA and s 74 of the Income Tax Act, punishable with a fine up to ZAR 5 million (or twice the amount of tax evaded) and imprisonment up to 5 years; if fraud is proven, common-law fraud charges may lead to up to 10 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in fraudulent tax filings or who fail to ensure SARS returns are submitted despite the company's insolvency can be held personally liable under s 158 of the TAA (for representative taxpayer liability) and s 22 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for reckless trade; SARS may issue a notice of personal liability, apply for a preservation order, obtain a civil judgement for the unpaid tax, and the director may face a travel ban via a foreign travel embargo under s 193 of the TAA; criminal conviction leads to imprisonment and disqualification from serving as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated royalty or management fees to the South African EMI, using a low-tax jurisdiction financing structure, providing non-arm's length loans with excessive interest rates, or making a deemed dividend distribution through excessive debt rather than declared dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may adjust the taxable income under section 31 to align with the arm's length principle; additional tax of up to 150% of the shortfall under a 'substantial understatement' penalty; interest at the prescribed rate; potential secondary transfer pricing adjustment recharacterising the funding as a dividend, giving rise to dividends tax at 20% on the non-resident; penalties for failure to maintain TP documentation (administrative penalty of up to ZAR 8,000 per month for each outstanding document, plus an understatement penalty).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign financial statements containing false TP declarations without reasonable care commit an offence under the Companies Act; joint liability with the company for the underpaid tax if the director knew of the wilful non-payment; the court may make a director liable for an amount equal to the tax, and under s 77 of the Companies Act a director is liable for losses suffered by the company arising from failure to exercise powers in accordance with the Act; travel restrictions apply in SARS's serious non-compliance procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a paper-only licensed EMI with no employees, no local decision-making, no physical office, and no treasury or risk management functions, while routing income to foreign related entities; such an arrangement stands as a sham or as a scheme without commercial substance under section 103.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may ignore the company's separate personality under the substance-over-form doctrine; disallow all associated deductions; reattribute the company's income directly to its beneficial owner, subjecting the income to tax and dividends tax; penalties for failure to register, publish returns, or maintain records (up to ZAR 4,000 per month per default); the company's bank licence may be revoked by the Prudential Authority for failure to satisfy the financial soundness requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors found to be knowingly party to a sham arrangement may be jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes under s 159 of the TAA (representative taxpayer liability); a court may pierce the corporate veil and hold the director personally accountable to SARS and creditors; a travel ban and criminal investigation under Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act may follow; sanctions include imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to ZAR 1 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an electronic money institution and effecting cross-border payments while failing to conduct customer due diligence (CDD), transaction monitoring, or reporting of suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC); processing funds for sanctioned persons or for unlicensed crypto/VASP activities connected to evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001: administrative fines up to ZAR 10 million per contravention (recently raised under General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022); remediation orders; suspension or removal of the EMI licence; criminal liability for directors who fail to report a suspicious transaction (imprisonment up to 15 years or fine up to ZAR 100 million for a corporate body); a court may additionally order forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director exercises control and management over the EMI's compliance function; under FIC Act s 46C, directors are personally liable where the company's failure is attributable to their fraud, negligence, or failure to act within their powers; the Prudential Authority must approve each director of an EMI, resulting in disqualification and a travel ban through the Financial Sector Conduct Authority; criminal imprisonment for up to 15 years is possible for individuals involved in money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold or Pay Dividends Tax / WHT over Interest and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident without withholding the statutory tax, or claiming treaty relief without a TRC/documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is liable for the withholding tax itself (withholding tax is a final tax borne by the company where it fails to withhold); 15%/20% unpaid amounts are recoverable by SARS with interest and penalties; SARS may charge an additional 100% penalty under s 210 of the TAA for failure to pay tax withheld; criminal sanctions apply for non-payment of the withheld amount within the prescribed period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow the company to pay dividends to non-residents without withholding are jointly and severally liable for the outstanding withholding tax and penalties as the company's representatives; travel bans under s 194 of the TAA may be issued, and imprisonment up to 5 years is possible for the intentional evasion of tax obligations.
